# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey tools that help businesses and individuals collect data from their audience. This comparison is particularly useful for those who value data ownership and are looking for a self-hosted solution, as the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is creating and sharing online forms, surveys, and quizzes.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Typeform offers a free plan with limited features, while Formbricks is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to have full control over their data, while Typeform stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Typeform has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be more scalable as it can be self-hosted on the user's own servers, while Typeform has limitations on the number of responses and users.
* Integration difference: Typeform has a wider range of integrations with third-party tools, while Formbricks has limited integrations but allows for custom development.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $25-$40/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $50-$100/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Typeform:**
* User-friendly interface
* Wide range of integrations
* Scalable pricing plans
* Limited control over data
* Cost can add up for large teams
**Formbricks:**
* Self-hosted and free
* Full control over data
* Customizable and scalable
* Limited integrations
* Requires technical expertise to set up

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who need a user-friendly interface and a wide range of integrations. It's also suitable for those who don't require full control over their data and are willing to pay for the convenience. On the other hand, Formbricks is ideal for larger teams or organizations that value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and customizing their own solution.

Formbricks is also a good choice for teams who require a high degree of customization and scalability, as it can be self-hosted on the user's own servers. Additionally, Formbricks is suitable for teams who are looking for a free and open-source solution, as it is licensed under the AGPL 3.0.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up your Formbricks instance on your own server.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to migrate your data from Typeform.
4. Customize and configure your Formbricks instance to fit your needs.
5. Test and deploy your new Formbricks instance.

## Our Take
Formbricks is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and customize. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Formbricks has limited support for certain types of conditional logic and branching. However, for teams who value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and customizing their own solution, Formbricks is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams who don't need a wide range of integrations
* Teams who value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and customizing their own solution
* Organizations with limited budgets who are looking for a free and self-hosted solution
* Teams who require a high degree of customization and scalability
* Developers who are looking for an open-source solution

## FAQ
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is free and self-hosted. However, you will need to pay for your own server costs.
### Is Formbricks suitable for large teams?
Yes, Formbricks can be suitable for large teams who value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and customizing their own solution.
### Can I migrate my Typeform data to Formbricks?
Yes, you can export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Formbricks using the Formbricks import tool.
### Does Formbricks have a user-friendly interface?
No, Formbricks requires technical expertise to set up and customize.
### Is Formbricks open-source?
Yes, Formbricks is licensed under the AGPL 3.0 and is open-source.

title: Miro vs Excalidraw
comparison_markdown:
# Miro vs Excalidraw

## Overview

Online collaborative whiteboard platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Excalidraw is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Miro costs Free / $8-$16/user/month; Excalidraw is Free
- **License**: Miro is Proprietary; Excalidraw is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Excalidraw can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Excalidraw eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Excalidraw has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Miro

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Excalidraw

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [excalidraw/excalidraw](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw) * ~90k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Miro if:** Miro is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Excalidraw if:** Excalidraw is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Miro in its standard export format, review Excalidraw import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Excalidraw is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Miro tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Excalidraw instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Miro, switching to self-hosted Excalidraw will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Miro until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Miro paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Excalidraw free to use?
Yes. Excalidraw is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Miro to Excalidraw?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Miro data, follow the Excalidraw import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Excalidraw get regular updates?
Yes. Excalidraw has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Excalidraw without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Excalidraw development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Miro](https://miro.com) and [Excalidraw](https://excalidraw.com) before making decisions.*

# Salesforce vs EspoCRM (2026)

## Overview
Salesforce and EspoCRM are two customer relationship management (CRM) tools that help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for businesses looking to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source alternative, with the core use case being sales team management and the key reason to switch being cost savings or data ownership.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Salesforce has a per-user monthly fee, while EspoCRM is free to use with self-hosting.
* Data Ownership: EspoCRM allows for full data ownership, while Salesforce has more restrictive data ownership policies.
* Setup Complexity: Salesforce has a more complex setup process, while EspoCRM is relatively easier to set up.
* Scalability: Salesforce is more scalable, with built-in support for large enterprises, while EspoCRM may require more manual configuration for large-scale deployments.
* Feature Difference: Salesforce has a built-in AI-powered sales forecasting tool, while EspoCRM relies on third-party integrations for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Salesforce | EspoCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1250-$15,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $5000-$60,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Salesforce:**
* Pros:
	+ Highly scalable and reliable
	+ Wide range of integrations and customizations available
	+ Strong customer support
	+ Advanced sales forecasting and analytics tools
* Cons:
	+ Expensive, especially for large teams
	+ Complex setup and configuration process
	+ Limited data ownership and control
**EspoCRM:**
* Pros:
	+ Free to use with self-hosting
	+ Full data ownership and control
	+ Highly customizable and extensible
	+ Active community and open-source development
* Cons:
	+ Limited scalability and performance for very large teams
	+ Requires technical expertise for setup and configuration
	+ Limited built-in integrations and customizations compared to Salesforce

## When to Choose Each
Salesforce is a good choice for large enterprises with complex sales and marketing operations, or for teams that require advanced sales forecasting and analytics tools. EspoCRM, on the other hand, is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses or teams that value data ownership and control, and are looking for a cost-effective, customizable CRM solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Salesforce data in CSV format using the Salesforce Data Export tool.
2. Prepare your EspoCRM instance by setting up the necessary modules and fields to match your Salesforce data.
3. Use the EspoCRM import tool to import your Salesforce data, mapping the fields and modules as necessary.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or customizations in EspoCRM to match your Salesforce setup.
5. Test and verify that your data has been successfully migrated and that your EspoCRM instance is functioning as expected.

## Our Take
EspoCRM is a production-ready CRM solution for most users, with a robust feature set and active community support. However, it's worth noting that EspoCRM may not be as polished or user-friendly as Salesforce, particularly for non-technical users. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that EspoCRM requires a decent amount of technical expertise to set up and configure, especially for large-scale deployments. Based on our analysis, we recommend switching to EspoCRM if you're a small to medium-sized business looking for a cost-effective, customizable CRM solution with full data ownership and control.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who don't need advanced sales forecasting tools
* Teams with simple sales and marketing operations who value data ownership and control
* Businesses with limited budgets who are looking for a cost-effective CRM solution
* Organizations with in-house technical expertise who can handle setup and configuration
* Companies with strict data privacy and security requirements who need full control over their CRM data

## FAQ
### Can I use EspoCRM for free?
Yes, EspoCRM is free to use with self-hosting, with no per-user fees or licensing costs.
### Is EspoCRM as scalable as Salesforce?
No, EspoCRM may not be as scalable as Salesforce for very large teams, but it can still handle small to medium-sized businesses with ease.
### Can I migrate my Salesforce data to EspoCRM?
Yes, you can export your Salesforce data in CSV format and import it into EspoCRM using the EspoCRM import tool.
### Does EspoCRM have the same level of customer support as Salesforce?
No, EspoCRM has a more limited level of customer support compared to Salesforce, but it has an active community and open-source development.
### Is EspoCRM compatible with my existing Salesforce integrations?
Not necessarily, EspoCRM may require new integrations or customizations to match your existing Salesforce setup.
